verdict: Red 6/10 ACCEPT-WITH-CUTS, blue 8/10 SUSTAINED - blue's conviction is higher than red's because every kill and every cut was re-verified against the primary Q1'26 release PDF. Three benches converge on FLAT into the 8/12 AMC print. The decisive finding is an evidence-chain failure on the thesis's own bull leg: the World Cup ASP collapse figures it built the print reconstruction on ($2,930 to $2,165, R32 -39%) do not appear in the Newsweek article it cites. The article tracks FIFA's PRIMARY portal medians via TicketData.com and never names StubHub. Blue sustained that kill with one honest reduction - the 1,774 to 10,547 supply jump IS in the article, so red overreached in calling the entire chain dead - but the ASP numbers are unsourced, and under the response taxonomy a fabricated or misattributed evidence chain is a data kill of the reconstruction, full stop. The second finding compounds it: the decline window is 22-29 June, which is inside Q2, and GMS books at transaction date rather than event date, so knockout resale transacts when matchups are known. The clean Q2/Q3 split the thesis needed does not exist - both quarters are World Cup contaminated in both directions, and the print direction is genuinely unresolvable pre-print with zero platform-specific data available. Third, and this is the sizing kill: the valuation omitted the senior claim. The Q1 balance sheet carries $454.4M of redeemable preferred with a $706.5M liquidation preference, and net income to common was $32.5M, not the $48.0M the thesis tabled - the standing rule to pull cap structure before any owner-earnings or yield claim was violated, and the '3.2% owner-earnings yield' is overstated. Blue reduced the severity correctly: the stack is being redeemed fast ($758.0M carrying and $1,027.6M liquidation preference at 12/31/25, plus a $100M May debt paydown), so this is a shrinking senior claim, not a static one, and interest expense is halving ($42.4M to $17.3M YoY). Fourth, the float trap is confirmed verbatim on both benches: $273.6M of the $298.4M of Q1 operating cash flow (92%) was customer float build, so ex-float FCF is roughly $17M/qtr against a headline of $290.6M. Fifth, crowding was understated - short interest is 11.82% of float (28.9M shares), not the 7.7% quoted, which is percent of shares outstanding. Blue closed red's one declared coverage gap and turned it into a finding: the claim that regulation cannot touch FY26 'at all' is refuted as an absolute - Maine's 10% service-fee cap has been effective since September 2025 and Vermont's 110% indie-venue cap since 2026-07-01 - though materiality is de minimis and the economic conclusion survives. Blue's best new finding is the bull-side one: Maine being live since Sept-2025 is a free natural experiment on the contagion-priced tail, and the take rate ROSE to 20.5% through two reported quarters with the cap in force. That is the first empirical contra-datum for the post-print cap-contagion court and it is the reason this is a park, not a permanent kill. STUB is covered (Citi et al.), so orphan discipline does not trigger; FLAT here is a no-position call, not a fair-value rejection. No forced seller or mechanism is named, so this is not a dislocation.
